evidence: UNVERIFIED: only source on Pantai Sauyas (Distrik Supiori Timur) mentions Pacific views and fishing, nothing on sand type or swimming - https://p2k.stekom.ac.id/ensiklopedia/Sauyas,_Supiori_Timur,_Supiori
Maluk Beach (white sand) bay is described as protected enough for swimming most of the year; nearby Jelenga is a surf break - https://www.backindo.com/?p=6386

UNVERIFIED: Pantai Sungai Bakau (15 km east of Kuala Pembuang) is cited as a white-sand river estuary, but no source on swimming and area noted as estuarine crocodile habitat - https://p2k.stekom.ac.id/ensiklopedia/Pantai_Sungai_Bakau

Pantai Cermin (Serdang Bedagai) has a stretch of white sand (https://ejurnal.its.ac.id/index.php/teknik/article/download/4717/1381); a family bathing (mandi) at Pantai Cermin was swept away by big waves, 8 dead - caveat: dangerous waves at times - https://m.jpnn.com/news/mandi-di-pantai-satu-keluarga-digulung-ombak-8-tewas

UNVERIFIED: no source found on sand or swimming at Pantai Kairatu or any SBB beach; search only returned Pantai Ora (Maluku Tengah, not SBB) - https://www.goodnewsfromindonesia.id/2026/01/28/pantai-ora-maluku-terkagum-dengan-magisnya-surga-pesisir-di-pulau-seram

Rote guide says the island has long, often empty beaches ideal for swimming, with sheltered bays at Oeseli; Nemberala itself is a white-sand reef surf beach (caveat: surf/reef at Nemberala) - https://www.backindo.com/rote-island/

Dodola Island (Morotai) has soft white sand, clear water and gentle waves; swimming and snorkeling listed as activities - https://rri.co.id/en/tourism/2720158/dodola-island-a-peaceful-tropical-escape-in-north-maluku

UNVERIFIED: Pantai Pohon Cinta (Marisa, Pohuwato) is a sunset spot; suitability study exists but no retrieved text on sand type or swimming - https://repository.ung.ac.id/get/karyailmiah/8466/Fitryane-Lihawa-Kajian-Analisis-Kesesuaian-Lahan-Wisata-Pantai-Pohon-Cinta-Dan-Pulau-Lahe.pdf

BPBD Penajam deploys personnel at regency beaches (incl. Corong) and urges visitors not to swim too far from shore (https://kaltim.antaranews.com/berita/235177/bpbd-penajam-sebar-personel-untuk-jaga-pengunjung-pantai-saat-libur-lebaran); Tanjung Jumlai (PPU) has fine white sand - https://www.suara.com/bestie/2023/10/06/061500/indahnya-barisan-pohon-kelapa-di-pantai-tanjung-jumlai-penajam-paser-utara
UNVERIFIED: Pantai Salu Kaili (Kec. Baras) is a developed tourist beach but no source on sand type or swimming - https://jurnal.undhirabali.ac.id/index.php/pariwisata/article/view/4826/4203

UNVERIFIED: Pantai Sirombu described only as a famous beautiful beach in Nias Barat; nothing on sand or swimming - https://repositori.uma.ac.id/jspui/bitstream/123456789/26224/1/198140033%20-%20Wiyu%20Fren%20Gulo%20-%20Fulltext.pdf
Pantai Somi (Kec. Gido, Kabupaten Nias) has a broad expanse of clean white sand and fairly calm waves suitable for swimming - https://repo.unias.ac.id/files/2025/3523/bab-iv.pdf
UNVERIFIED: Pantai Sisi (Serasan, Natuna) has white sand and a sea described as calm like a pool, but no source explicitly states swimming - https://dinaspariwisata.natunakab.go.id/?p=161

UNVERIFIED: Pantai Naga Permai (Suak Puntong, Kuala Pesisir) is the most-visited beach but source covers abrasion and waste only, not sand or swimming - https://jurnal.utu.ac.id/mkreatif/article/view/4654
UNVERIFIED: no web source found on Pantai Pajala or other Muna Barat beaches - no URL

BPBD Mukomuko warns beach visitors to be careful when bathing (mandi) at the beach in extreme weather (https://megapolitan.antaranews.com/berita/377149/mukomuko-imbau-wisatawan-waspadai-cuaca-ekstrem); Pantai Pandan Wangi has a clean sand expanse lined with cemara - caveat: wave/weather warnings - https://www.goodnewsfromindonesia.id/2024/12/20/daftar-pantai-di-bengkulu-lengkap-dengan-alamat-htm-dan-daya-tarik
UNVERIFIED: no web source found on Pantai Ungkea or other Morowali Utara beaches - no URL
UNVERIFIED: Pantai Puluti (Desa Lahuafu, Bungku Tengah) has white sand and greenish water, but no source on swimming - https://kumparan.com/paluposo/pesona-pasir-putih-di-pantai-puluti-1sBzlEV9StX
Pantai Waecicu (Labuan Bajo) has white sands and calm waves suitable for beginner swimmers (reviews also note trash and fees) - https://wanderlog.com/place/details/1973377/pantai-waecicu
UNVERIFIED: Pantai Abudenok (Malaka Barat) has a ~400 m fine-sand shore used for sand sports, but no source on swimming - https://ejournal.upg45ntt.ac.id/jss/article/download/90/59
